default_prompt: You are screening a record for a systematic review of randomized controlled trials on perioperative variables in spine surgery. Read the title and abstract and decide whether the record should be included, applying this review's published eligibility criteria (SYNERGY dataset; original review DOI 10.1097/BRS.0000000000003645): the study must be an RCT with a 1:1 parallel two-arm design; related to spine surgery involving preoperative, intraoperative, or postoperative variables; and have a dichotomous primary or secondary outcome. Exclude studies not involving human subjects, studies with continuous-variable outcomes (e.g. pain scores, Oswestry Disability Index scores, time to union) without predefined clinical success criteria, and studies that did not report a statistically significant primary or secondary outcome measure.
_notes: One of 3 per-review config files (runbook §2, §6) -- vendors/aggregation/tau/
zero_policy/confidence_threshold are identical across all three by design
(the same fixed instrument, screening a different review each run); only
default_prompt differs. See ../README.md for the full history/rationale behind
every other field (tau derivation, model pinning, temperature, zero_policy, the
track_prompts -> default_prompt migration) -- not duplicated here to avoid
three copies going stale independently.

This file is not read literally beyond 'vendors' (including each
vendor's 'temperature'), 'aggregation', 'tau', 'zero_policy',
'default_prompt', 'track_prompts' (unused here), and
'confidence_threshold' (see attest.cli._load_ensemble_config) -- this
_notes field is ignored by the loader and safe to keep as documentation.
'batch_size' (attest.provenance.config.Config.batch_size, "b_e") is
deliberately absent from this checked-in template: it must equal the
exact number of records attest's own prefilter keeps from this run's
data/gold.json, which depends on whichever synergy-dataset version
built it, so it is not a number this file can safely hand-carry.
`make resolved-config` (src/resolve_batch_size.py) patches it in at
build time, writing data/config.resolved.json -- the file `attest
screen` actually reads (see Makefile). Do not add a literal
'batch_size' here; a stale hardcoded value would only be silently
overwritten by the patch step, or worse, mislead a reader of this file.
